91:4928.name: Badge
91:4928.description:
A small status indicator badge with two presentation types: a simple dot indicator or a text badge. It supports semantic variants (Default/Info/Success/Warning/Error) and a single size (sm) in the current set.

PURPOSE: Indicate a lightweight status/notification signal (e.g., unread, warning, success) attached to another UI element such as an avatar, nav item, or setting.

BEHAVIOR: Not interactive in the provided structure; it is a purely visual indicator.

COMPOSITION: No nested component instances detected. Internally each variant is either a single ELLIPSE (Dot type) or a single TEXT layer (Text type).

USAGE: Use Dot when space is constrained or when the exact count/label is not needed. Use Text when a count or short label is required. Prefer semantic variants to match the meaning (Info/Success/Warning/Error) rather than using color alone.

CODE GENERATION NOTES: Implement as a small inline element with two render modes (dot vs text). Ensure semantic variants map to design tokens for background/text color. For Text type, enforce max width/overflow rules (e.g., 99+), and ensure accessible labeling when used without visible text (Dot).

53:2775.name: Button
53:2775.description:
A configurable button component set with visual variants (Primary/Secondary/Tertiary/Bare) and interactive states (Default/Hover/Active/Focus/Disabled). It supports optional leading and trailing icon slots via nested icon instances and boolean slot toggles.

PURPOSE: Provide a standard clickable control for triggering actions, with consistent styling across emphasis levels (Primary → Bare).

BEHAVIOR: Supports common interaction states: Hover (pointer over), Active (pressed), Focus (keyboard focus with a visible focus outline layer), and Disabled (non-interactive). Slot Before/After booleans indicate optional icon placement around the label.

COMPOSITION: Nested component instances used: "Icon Before" (INSTANCE), "Icon After" (INSTANCE). Also contains a "Label" frame with a text node, and a "Focus Outline" rectangle layer in Focus state variants. Code generators should check the codebase for existing icon components that correspond to these instances before creating new icon primitives.

USAGE: Use Primary for the main call-to-action, Secondary for less prominent actions, Tertiary/Bare for low-emphasis or inline/toolbar contexts. Use Slot Before/After for contextual icons (e.g., download, external link) while keeping the label text for clarity.

CODE GENERATION NOTES: Implement as a single Button component with props mapping to Variant/State and optional start/end icons. Ensure focus-visible styling matches the Focus Outline layer (likely an outline/ring). Disabled should block pointer/keyboard activation and apply disabled styling. Icon instances imply a consistent icon size and alignment; preserve spacing between icon and label and ensure icons inherit currentColor where appropriate.
